Calculate distances for fixed neighbor indices

Source: R/knn-utils.R
knn_distances.Rd

Calculate distances for the supplied indices in their existing order. Rows of idx correspond to observations, or to queries when query is supplied. Indices always refer to observations in data. Missing indices (0) remain paired with NA distances.

Usage

knn_distances(
  data,
  idx,
  metric = "euclidean",
  query = NULL,
  n_threads = 0,
  verbose = FALSE,
  obs = "R"
)

Arguments

data

Reference observations, in a numeric matrix or data frame, a logical matrix, or a numeric sparse matrix.

idx

Numeric matrix of whole-number neighbor indices. For a graph, pass graph$idx.

metric

Distance metric, evaluated directly. See brute_force_knn().

query

Optional query observations with the same feature layout as data. Query and reference must both be sparse or both dense, and their logical or numeric storage must match. Logical features cannot be NA.

n_threads

Number of threads to use. Zero runs serially.

verbose

Whether to report progress.

obs

Whether observations are in rows ("R") or columns ("C").

Value

A list containing the supplied idx and calculated dist matrices.

Examples

graph <- brute_force_knn(iris[1:8, 1:4], k = 5)
knn_distances(iris[1:8, 1:4], graph$idx, metric = "manhattan")
#> $idx
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5]
#> [1,]    1    5    8    3    7
#> [2,]    2    3    4    8    7
#> [3,]    3    4    7    2    8
#> [4,]    4    3    2    7    8
#> [5,]    5    1    8    7    3
#> [6,]    6    5    1    8    7
#> [7,]    7    3    4    8    5
#> [8,]    8    1    5    3    2
#> 
#> $dist
#>      [,1]      [,2]      [,3]      [,4]      [,5]
#> [1,]    0 0.1999998 0.2999998 0.8000001 0.6999999
#> [2,]    0 0.5000004 0.5000001 0.6000000 0.8000003
#> [3,]    0 0.4000001 0.5000000 0.5000004 0.7000003
#> [4,]    0 0.4000001 0.5000001 0.5000002 0.7000003
#> [5,]    0 0.1999998 0.2999998 0.6999999 0.8000001
#> [6,]    0 1.2000004 1.2000004 1.3000002 1.7000003
#> [7,]    0 0.5000000 0.5000002 0.6000001 0.6999999
#> [8,]    0 0.2999998 0.2999998 0.7000003 0.6000000
#>
